To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pic and setBA genes of Shigella and enteroaggressive E. coli are transcribed in overlapping fashion, that the pic and the setB gene are regulated differently, that the setB promoter lies upstream of setB, and that the intestinal environment provides a strong signal to relieve setB silencing.
(i) the setBA and pic genes are expressed as two complementary 4-kDa transcripts, and (ii) setBA expression is regulated by a complex set of factors including temperature and anaerobiosis.
The overlapping set/pic locus in Shigella and enteroaggressive E. coli encodes an enterotoxin, ShET1, and a mucinase, Pic, which are both required for virulence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of virulence in enteropathogenic bacteria and, in particular, the regulation of the overlapping set locus.
the genetic regulation and the role of the Shigella enterotoxin (Set).
the regulation of a virulence locus that is highly conserved in two pathogenic strains of Escherichia col i.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pic and setBA loci in Shigella and EAggEC are transcribed as two independent 4-kb transcripts, that the pic promoter is activated at 37° and that the setBA promoter is silenced by its own leader sequence.
pic and setBA genes are transcribed as two separate mRNAs, with setBA being repressed by a long leader sequence and relieved by some unknown signals.
the pic/setBA locus is transcribed as a single 4.2-kb mRNA species, with the setB structural and setBA promoter genes transcribed from the opposite strand of pic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pic locus is expressed at high levels in exponential growth phase at 37°C, whereas the setBA locus is expressed only at very low levels in exponential phase and is expressed at high level in anaerobic continuous culture.
ShET1 is expressed in vivo, and the expression is regulated by a complex mechanism which is influenced by the host environment.
the setB locus is regulated in a complex fashion and may be activated in vivo by signals present in the human intestine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ShET1 is a highly conserved virulence factor in Shigella and EAggEC, and that it is expressed in the intestinal lumen, but not in the host cell cytoplasm.
ShET1 expression is repressed in most environments, but is activated in the intestine, suggesting that ShET1 production may be an adaptive response of the pathogen.
the setB locus is subject to complex regulation and may be expressed in vivo in the human intestine.
